logp.method_description: The partition coefficient (Pow) is defined as Pow = corg/caq, where corg and caq are the molar concentrations of the compound in the organic and aqueous phases, respectively. Pow was determined by the shake-flask method and UV–vis measurements. Deionized water and n-octanol were shaken in a large glass bottle in a planar shaker for 24 h to enable saturation of both phases and then separated by centrifugation (5000 rpm, 5 min). A stock solution of the selected compound (5 mM) was prepared by first adding DMF. The solution was diluted with octanol-saturated water to give a final concentration of 5 μM (so that 0.8 ≤ A ≤ 1.5 at λmax) and its UV-vis spectrum was recorded (A0aq). An aliquot of the solution (Vaq = 4.0 mL) was transferred into a test tube, and water-saturated octanol (Vorg = Vaq = 4.0 mL) was added. The mixture was shaken for 1 h at room temperature and then centrifuged (5000 rpm, 5 min). The UV-visible spectrum of the aqueous phase was recorded (Afaq). Subsequently, the partition coefficient was calculated as Pow = (A0aq - Afaq)/Afaq, where A0aq and Afaq are the absorbances of the aqueous phase before and after partitioning with the organic phase, respectively. The procedure was repeated three times for each sample; the results are shown as mean ± standard deviation (Table S6).
